title: fine-print writes the same PDF: raw byte identity, or identity after canon()

contract.summary: The writer, end to end. A row with no deflate anywhere is strict byte identity (raw tier); a row with any FlateDecode stream is identity after canon() (SPEC section 3), because three runtimes ship three deflaters and the file ID is an md5 over the compressed body. artifacts.pdf is PHP's raw PDF (raw tier) or its canon() (canon tier), for diffing a failure.

functions.toBytes: toBytes(doc, options) -> fingerprint(pdf, input.tier): raw {tier, sha256, length, canonSha256} | canon {tier, canonSha256, canonLength}

contract.referenceNote: Run on PHP 8.4 by the exporter. Canon-tier goldens never carry a raw hash: PHP's own deflate differs between zlib builds.

notes: Rows are EXPORTED from PHP by fine-print/tests/Conformance/Export.php (composer conformance:export) and are never edited by hand or regenerated by a port. fine-print's DriftTest re-exports to a temporary directory and fails if anything here moved.

No discrimination probe for the writer itself lives here: the implementation under test is a PDF writer, which this package does not carry (the same known gap as flow/graph-runs). canon() IS small enough to carry: tests/fine-print-canon.test.ts re-implements it independently of the exporter, checks it against every writer-bytes artifact, and pins its mutants.
